blocks.text: CALASIAO, Pangasinan — The clash between the Super El Niño and the northeast monsoon, or “amihan,” is bringing cooler nights and scorching daytime temperatures to Pangasinan, where the heat index has reached 40°C and above. The unusual weather pattern is associated with the shear line, a meteorological boundary where contrasting air masses meet. The interaction can cause changes in wind direction and bring heavy rainfall and thunderstorms. According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), shear lines commonly form when the northeast monsoon interacts with warmer air from the Pacific.
